rationale: The assistant immediately told the customer to stop using and unplug the microwave, avoided opening the casing, and correctly identified the burnt waveguide cover as the likely cause, with replacement as the fix. It leaned a little too heavily on professional fitting, since a clip-on cover is an acceptable DIY replacement. It also did not clearly say to clean the cavity of the old splatter after replacing the cover, and it did not name the exact part as a purchasable item for the known model. Its advice overall is safe and useful.
